source.title: The Dragon Hatchling: The Missing Link between the Transformer and Models of the Brain
source.authors: A. Kosowski; Przemyslaw Uznanski; J. Chorowski; Zuzanna Stamirowska; M. Bartoszkiewicz

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study discusses monosemanticity and reports concept-selective synapses in BDH-GPU, but it does not measure whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs or otherwise test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports concept-selective synapse results and sparse neuron activations. Synapse selectivity is not a measurement of neuron polysemanticity, and activation sparsity does not measure how many unrelated inputs a neuron responds to. These related synapse results are recorded as versions ["none"]; the other architecture, performance, and sparsity results do not bear directly on the claim. Cited findings from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces the BDH/BDH-GPU architecture and reports concept-selective 'monosemantic synapses' (entries of the attention state matrix σ) and activation sparsity. It never measures how many neurons respond to unrelated inputs, never compares polysemantic-neuron shares across architectures, and never tests superposition or measurement choices. Synapse selectivity and sparsity are related but different constructs, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct: the authors claim BDH-GPU shows 'monosemanticity' via concept-selective synapses and sparse positive activations, and Table 3 asserts only possible monosemantic neurons in Transformers. They do not quantify neuron polysemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates a different architecture and measures concept-selective synapses, not the original neuron-response phenomenon.

fits_no_version.finding: A selected BDH-GPU 'currency synapse' scores higher on 50 generated currency sentences than on 50 politics sentences (U=2368/2500, rank-biserial 0.86), and responds across French and English.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual attention-state entries (synapses) in BDH-GPU can be concept-selective across languages.

fits_no_version.finding: BDH-GPU y-activations are sparse (about 5%; 2.5–7.5% in layer 2 of a synthetic task), sparser for predictable input.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ReLU-based positive high-dimensional activations in BDH-GPU are sparse, which the authors link to interpretability.

record.problems: The synapse examples were identified by searching for entries predictive of a concept, and the statistical test concerns one selected currency synapse and generated sentence sets. The paper does not assess neuron-level polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted that directly bear on the claim. The paper's neuron-sparsity and language-model performance results do not measure neuron polysemanticity.

untested.parts: No transformer MLP neurons examined for responses to unrelated tokens.
No test of superposition or capacity pressure as a cause.
No test of polysemanticity without capacity pressure.
No polysemantic-neuron share measured for BDH-GPU or compared with GPT baselines; the 'monosemantic' claim concerns synapses, not a neuron-share comparison.
No reassessment of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No variation of activation range or explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's 'monosemanticity' language could mislead a search into treating it as V5 evidence (architecture lowers polysemanticity), but no neuron-level polysemanticity rate is measured in BDH-GPU or the GPT baseline, so it does not test V5. Synapses were found by searching for predictive entries; the statistical test uses ChatGPT-generated sentences.

versions.untested_parts: No image-classifier neurons or visual inputs are studied.
No transformer MLP neurons are tested for responses to unrelated tokens or contexts.
The study does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
The study does not test neuron polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
The study does not compare polysemantic-neuron shares across architectures or activation functions, or measure whether that share can be reduced without performance loss.
The study does not reassess canonical polysemantic neurons or test whether their mixed responses reflect a shared feature.
The study does not vary activation-range selection or explanation-scoring methods for measuring neuron polysemanticity.

rows.subject: BDH-GPU model
rows.operation_detail: Compared currency-synapse values between currency-related sentences and politics sentences without currency mentions.

conditions.value: 50 ChatGPT-generated European-currency sentences versus 50 European-politics sentences without currency mentions

rows.measure: Currency synapse values; one-sided Mann–Whitney U test and rank-biserial correlation
rows.note: This tests selectivity of a synapse, not polysemanticity of neurons; the authors state that the currency-related sentences received significantly higher currency-synapse values.
rows.check: Measures selectivity of one chosen σ-matrix entry (synapse), not neuron polysemanticity; the synapse was selected for its predictive power, so the contrast is partly circular. Link to none is correct; state relative to the claim cannot be determined.

relation.reason: The paper discusses monosemanticity (synapses in BDH, possible monosemantic neurons in Transformers in Table 3) but does not test neuron polysemanticity or cite its sources.

tranche.reason: Measures concept-selective synapses (sigma-matrix entries) and activation sparsity in a new architecture. It never measures how many neurons respond to unrelated inputs, so it bears on no version, V5 included.

source_check.notes: Evidence is at the synapse level only (U = 2368 of Uopt = 2500, rank-biserial 0.86, p < 10^-14, on 50 vs 50 ChatGPT sentences; model n = 49152, d = 256, 4 heads, 8 layers per Appendix B.3). There is no neuron-level polysemanticity measure. The synapse was chosen for predictive power on Europarl sentences, and the test sentences were generated separately.
